Hi Bryan — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary from our call
- Primary workload: clinician-facing summarization and PHI extraction from visit notes (low latency, regulated).
- Traffic profile: spiky during clinic hours; baseline ~30 req/s, peaks ~220 req/s.
- Data residency: US-only, SOC 2 + HIPAA posture required.
- Concern: noisy-neighbor effects when shared pools see bursty customers; need clarity on isolation and SLO guarantees.

Where we think you land (qualification)
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) looks closest to requirements given latency predictability + isolation.
- Private VPC or on-prem could be required if procurement/legal insists on customer-managed network and HSM.
- Hosted API is attractive for speed-to-market but would need contractual SLOs and stronger isolation features to meet your compliance bar.

Specific infra questions you raised (we committed to answer)
1) How do you prevent noisy neighbor interference across tenants?
2) What latency SLOs can you guarantee on Dedicated vs Hosted? How does fallback work when capacity is constrained?
3) How does cache warming / cold-start behavior affect tail latency for real-time calls?
4) If we start Hosted, can we move to Dedicated/Private without re-architecting prompts or onboarding?

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- Technical deep-dive / architecture workshop with Grace (runtime lead) — 60 min. Objective: show isolation controls, routing, KV cache behavior. (Target week of Jul 20)
- Provide a scoped capacity analysis and exemplar costs for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — attached: capacity_analysis_stub.xlsx
- Share SOC 2 summary and template enterprise terms for review — attached: SOC2_summary.pdf, enterprise_terms_draft.docx
- Run an initial POC proposal: 2-week burst on Dedicated with model variant fallback & monitoring.

Please confirm which items you want prioritized (workshop vs procurement paperwork vs POC). I can loop in solutions engineering if you want a rapid proof-of-concept.

Thanks,

Thanks for the context, Bryan — quick technical note for your security packet and procurement: 

Noisy-neighbor mitigations (summary)
- Dedicated pools: tenant-exclusive GPU allocation with isolated runtime processes; kernel-level QoS controls to limit cross-tenant scheduling interference; eviction policies for long-running batches. This yields predictable p95/p99 tails under typical clinic-hour bursts.
- Hosted pools: multi-tenant scheduler with per-tenant weight-based slotting, prefix/KV caching controls, and soft isolation. We offer tenant-priority lanes for customers on higher tiers to reduce interference risk.

Fallback & auditing
- Automatic fallback: when Dedicated capacity hits a configurable threshold, requests can be routed to (1) a lower-cost, smaller model variant on the same Dedicated pool, or (2) a matched Hosted pool in the same region. Transition is performed by policy rules; every routed request is tagged and logged with routing reason and model_variant_id.
- Auditability: routing decisions and request metadata (request_id, model_variant_id, fallback_reason) are persisted to the customer's audit stream and are available in Console logs with 90-day retention (longer retention available as add-on).

Latency SLOs (examples)
- Dedicated (reserved GPUs): p50: 45ms, p95: 180ms, p99: 420ms (for standard-1024 token prompts on our L2 optimized runtime).
- Hosted (shared): p50: 55ms, p95: 260ms, p99: 700ms (variance depends on regional pool utilization & caching).

Cache & cold-starts
- KV cache warming: Dedicated pools support pinned KV cache for hot prefixes; warming scripts can pre-load frequent cohorts to reduce tail latency. Cold-starts are rare for warmed endpoints; worst-case model-load for a quantized model is ~1.2s but mitigated by pre-warmed workers for reserved capacity.

I'll attach a small routing diagram and a one-paragraph blurb you can paste into procurement materials.

—Grace
